Name: S01
Title: Welcome to the XRLibraries Campus
Body: Three galleries and the Wax Hall tell XRLibraries’ story. After the museum, the tour visits the reading room, the four workshop rooms of the school and the Recess Yard. Margaret, the guide by the door, answers questions anytime.

Name: S02
Title: Over 200 VR Systems in California Libraries
Body: XRLibraries began in 2016 by installing more than 200 virtual reality systems in California public libraries. Its website calls this the largest VR installation in public libraries.

Name: S03
Title: XR Made Easy for Everyone
Body: XRLibraries works with schools and libraries to bring virtual, augmented and mixed reality into their programs and classes. Its stated goal is equitable access to immersive technology for all communities.

Name: S04
Title: A Library VR Headset
Body: Standalone headsets let a library visitor stand on the moon, swim a coral reef or practice a job, with no computer attached. Meta Quest and Pico both appear on XRLibraries’ partner list, and its Nevada headsets run on Pico.

Name: S05
Title: Nevada Follows Marin County
Body: In 2017 Nevada’s state library put its first VR headsets in public libraries: 22 headsets in 11 libraries, with STEM content. WorkingNation reports that the model followed a program at the Marin County Free Library in California.

Name: S06
Title: XR at Computers in Libraries
Body: XRLibraries’ executive director, John MacLeod, presented “Integrating XR Tech & Programming in Libraries” at Computers in Libraries Connect in 2020 and “Using XR to Discover ‘Lost Stories’ & Pop-Up Books” in 2022.

Name: S07
Title: Project SANDI
Body: Supporting and Advancing Nevada’s Dislocated Individuals began during the 2020 downturn with a $13.8 million federal grant. It uses VR to explore careers in five fields: skilled trades, healthcare, IT, advanced manufacturing and logistics.

Name: S08
Title: 1,100 Headsets in Nevada
Body: XRLibraries and Lifeliqe installed VR headsets in Nevada’s community college and public libraries. XRLibraries’ homepage counts more than 1,100.

Name: S09
Title: Training From a Town of 300
Body: A remote 12-week dialysis technician certification lets people train without traveling to a training center. In a community of about 300 people, a single mother finished the program, passed her certification and plans to become a registered nurse.

Name: S10
Title: XR Playbooks
Body: XRLibraries catalogs more than 300 XR apps in categories from astronomy and history to mindfulness and music, then bundles them into themed playbooks that come pre-installed on library headsets.

Name: S11
Title: XR Showcase
Body: In this video series, hosts George and Camila try VR and AR apps for libraries, from Tilt Brush and Wander to Apollo 11 VR, and share practical tips like cleaning headsets and setting a guardian boundary.

Name: S12
Title: A Way Out of No Way
Body: Marin City students who call themselves the Marinovators built a VR experience of the World War II shipyards and life in Marin City, plus a musical tribute to the African-American workers whose stories were rarely told.

Name: S13
Title: The Black Wall Street of Charleston
Body: Career and technical education students at Burke High School built an augmented-reality scavenger hunt that leads players to Charleston’s Black-owned businesses.

Name: S14
Title: Seeking Immortality
Body: A browser-based VR world, funded by an IMLS Native American Enhancement Grant, that preserves endangered Cheyenne language and cultural knowledge. Tribal members and students learned 3D scanning so the tribe keeps control of its own data.

Name: S15
Title: Children Draw War, Not Flowers
Body: An immersive 3D exhibition of art by children in Ukraine’s Cherkasy region, which took in more than 42,000 displaced children. It helps children work through war-related trauma, preserves their artwork, and was honored at the Anthem Awards.

Name: S16
Title: Pollinators at the Marin County Fair
Body: At XRLibraries’ bug-themed booth, fairgoers used an AR app called Pollinators to plant flowers and release monarch butterflies that flew around pollinating them. Marin artist Cynthia Jensen lent bug sculptures for the booth.

Name: S17
Title: The Wax Hall
Body: Through the doorway at the end of Gallery 3, wax figures act out XRLibraries’ story in twelve scenes, from the first VR stations in 2016 to the 2025 Marin County Fair. Each scene comes to life as you walk up. The figures are reenactors, not likenesses of real people.

Name: S18
Title: The First Headsets
Body: In 2016, libraries in Marin County, California, began offering virtual reality stations as the pilot for the California Virtual Reality Experience. XRLibraries launched that year as the project’s coordinator. Teen volunteers helped first-time visitors into headsets and guided them through their first worlds.

Name: S19
Title: VR Goes Statewide
Body: In June 2017 the California State Library, Oculus and the library consortium Califa partnered to bring VR-ready PCs with Rift headsets to more than 90 libraries across California, building on the Marin County pilot. XRLibraries, launched in 2016 as the project’s coordinator, also became a clearinghouse where libraries share what works with VR and AR.

Name: S20
Title: Story Time in 3D
Body: Library Journal reported in 2017 that young children loved virtual reality story times, while teens gravitated to VR games. In Marin, children listened to stories inside three-dimensional worlds.

Name: S21
Title: Nevada Opens Its Stations
Body: Nevada’s state library set aside $22,000 of a 2017 budget increase for a VR pilot: 22 headsets loaded with STEM content in 11 libraries, modeled on Marin County’s program. In February 2018 the Carson City Library’s grand re-opening featured VR and AR stations, and XRLibraries’ founder presented in a webinar for librarians across the state.

Name: S22
Title: VR on the Road
Body: Marin’s VR program went out into the community: to schools, senior centers, the county fair, and people displaced by deadly wildfires.

Name: S23
Title: VR in the World’s Catalog
Body: Nevada’s state library and its partner XRLibraries set out to catalog VR content so any library could find it. In 2019 Nevada librarians led a first-of-its-kind effort to catalog virtual reality in WorldCat, the world’s largest library catalog, and planned a cataloging hack-a-thon in Marin, California and Carson City, Nevada.

Name: S24
Title: XR Marin and the XR Stars
Body: XR Marin brought together the Marin County Free Library, XRLibraries, Novato Unified School District and the Marin County Office of Education. Teens served as “XR Stars,” helping patrons use the equipment. Its programs let people make 3D models, design 3D games and produce 360-degree video tours, and one teen at a VR summer camp borrowed the cameras and filmed her family’s farm.

Name: S25
Title: Project SANDI
Body: In October 2020 Nevada won a $13.8 million federal grant for Project SANDI (Supporting and Advancing Nevada’s Dislocated Individuals), which uses VR to explore careers in skilled trades, healthcare, IT, advanced manufacturing and logistics. It grew to more than 1,000 headsets at over 80 locations. XRLibraries’ executive director is a partner in the project.

Name: S26
Title: 360° Stories in Washington
Body: XRLibraries was the trainer for the Washington State Library’s VR 360 grant program. In 2022 it helped six libraries create 360-degree virtual reality stories about topics important to their communities. The program was open to public, tribal and academic libraries and funded by IMLS through the Library Services and Technology Act.

Name: S27
Title: Lost Stories
Body: In Marin City, students who call themselves the Marinovators built a VR experience of the World War II shipyards and life in Marin City, plus a musical tribute to the African-American workers whose stories were rarely told. XRLibraries’ director presented its Lost Stories work at Computers in Libraries in 2022.

Name: S28
Title: Children Draw War, Not Flowers
Body: XRLibraries helped design “Children Draw War, Not Flowers,” a browser-based VR art exhibition from the San José State University School of Information. It shows art by Ukrainian children aged 4 to 16 and virtual galleries showing the destruction of Ukrainian libraries, and anyone can visit it free in a web browser.

Name: S29
Title: Pollinators at the Fair
Body: At the 2025 Marin County Fair, XRLibraries’ bug-themed booth featured Pollinators, an augmented-reality app where fairgoers planted flowers and released monarch butterflies that flew around pollinating them. Marin artist Cynthia Jensen lent bug sculptures for the booth.

Name: S30
Title: The Reading Room
Body: The library has 15 short books about XR and more, open to read on the featured table and on the ends of the stacks. Rosa at the reference desk answers questions from them.

Name: S31
Title: Room 101: 3D Art Studio
Body: Every class in the Workshop School is a hands-on workshop. Here you paint in the air with neon, chrome, ribbon and rainbow brushes, stamp 3D shapes, mirror your strokes and switch to a blank canvas.

Name: S32
Title: Room 102: Science Lab
Body: A working lab with goggles on. Run a sieve analysis to measure the grain sizes in a sand sample, find the concentration of a mystery acid by titration, and measure gravity with a pendulum.

Name: S33
Title: Room 103: Blueprint Lab
Body: Five real-world blueprints: a car, an excavator, a house, a truss bridge and a computer. Tap any part to learn its name, what it does and how you could build a model, then build a model car or building at the bench.

Name: S34
Title: Room 104: World Builder Studio
Body: How do you build a world like this campus? Build a mini world on the layer table one step at a time, from a sketch to a live website, and read the World Builder’s Handbook to start your own.

Name: S35
Title: The Recess Yard
DateLabel: Out the back of the school
Body: Recess is for fun in XR: ride the Comet Coaster, take the Sky Drop for a view of the whole campus, or go on an Ocean Dive with sea creatures. Coach Rae can help, and XR tokens are hidden all over the campus.
